study_identification_part.si4_title: Regional, circuit and network heterogeneity of brain abnormalities in psychiatric disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the multiscale heterogeneity of gray matter volume differences in psychiatric disorders using normative modeling. It investigated whether anatomically heterogeneous regional gray matter volume deviations are functionally coupled to common areas and networks.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-based permutation tests (shuffling group labels) for regional, circuit-level, and network-level overlap differences; Spatial permutation tests for circuit-level and network-level overlap differences (preserving deviation burden); FDR-corrected threshold (P FDR < 0.05, two-tailed) for statistical significance.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Extreme regional heterogeneity of GMV deviations is a general characteristic of mental illness, but these deviations are often coupled to common functional circuits and networks, providing a neural substrate for phenotypic similarities.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Regional GMV deviations showed marked individual heterogeneity, with maximum overlap in any single region never exceeding 7% (e.g., MDD: 6.21%). However, these regionally heterogeneous deviations were often embedded within common functional circuits and networks, with circuit-level overlap reaching up to 53% in clinical groups (e.g., SCZ), significantly higher than regional overlap. Group-based permutation tests revealed significantly greater circuit-level overlap across large cortical areas for SCZ (~75%) and MDD (~31%). Network-level analysis showed SCZ and MDD had greater overlap across multiple networks, with the salience/ventral attention network being implicated transdiagnostically across five of six disorders. Spatial permutation tests indicated that much of this elevated overlap was driven by total deviation burden, though some preferential targeting was observed for SCZ (salience/ventral attention network) and ADHD (dorsal attention/medial temporal networks). Positive GMV deviations showed less overlap but ASD exhibited elevated circuit- and network-level overlap under group-based permutation testing, mainly due to increased positive GMV burden.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Considerable overlap between cases and controls due to low deviation burden in ~50% of clinical participants; limited sensitivity of MRI-derived GMV estimates; pooling multisite data with varied protocols; limited scope for investigating correlations with symptom profiles or other clinical variables; reliance on DSM/ICD diagnoses rather than specific syndromes.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: While deviation burden was higher in cases than controls, and most people showed at least one deviation, a substantial fraction of clinical participants (~50%) showed a relatively low deviation burden (<3 deviations). This result implies that there is considerable overlap between cases and controls...; The result may also reflect the limited sensitivity of MRI-derived GMV estimates to map pathophysiologically relevant brain changes.; Sample sizes in single-site psychiatric neuroimaging studies are often small, so we pooled data from multiple sites... data were collected with different acquisition, recruitment and clinical assessment protocols.; investigating correlations with symptom profiles or other clinically relevant variables such as age of onset, illness duration, medication exposure or disease severity across disorders was beyond our scope.; Our cases were diagnosed according to Diagnostic Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) or the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) criteria... focusing on specific syndromes rather than traditional diagnoses... may yield a more precise mapping...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Adaptation of lesion network mapping for use with normative modeling to characterize neural heterogeneity across regional, circuit, and network levels; use of spatial permutation tests to distinguish deviation burden from preferential accumulation of pathology; emphasis on patient-specific brain changes and network context for tailored interventions.
